Egyptian gang robs moving truck and steals 105 kilograms of frozen chicken.
A six-member criminal gang in Egypt carried out a bizarre highway robbery, stealing 105 kilograms of frozen chicken from a truck while it was still moving on the Cairo-Ismailia Desert Road.

Footage shows men climbing onto the front of a pickup truck, opening the rear doors of the moving refrigerated truck and passing boxes of chicken to their accomplices. The truck was carrying around four tons of poultry, and the driver reportedly did not realize the theft was happening.

Police later tracked down the six suspects. According to Egypt’s Interior Ministry, the group had previous criminal records and opened fire when police attempted to arrest them. Three suspects were killed in the resulting shootout, while the other three were arrested. Weapons, the getaway vehicle and stolen goods were recovered.
The footage has gone viral online, with users comparing the robbery to a scene from Fast & Furious.

“Don’t fight-because nobody wins.”
A popular saying used by police and legal educators is:
“If you win, you go to jail. If you lose, you go to the hospital.” The message is simple: physical fights can create serious consequences for everyone involved.

Under Chinese law, even a person who starts or wins a fight may face legal consequences if the incident causes injury or is considered a violation of public order. The person who loses may suffer physical harm, medical costs, and further legal disputes.

This reflects a broader emphasis on maintaining public order in a country with a very large population.
Ot course, disagreements and contlicts still happen everywhere-including China. But many people are aware that public fights can quickly escalate into legal problems, financial losses, and long-term consequences.
Sometimes the strongest move is not throwing a punch.
It’s walking away.
Do you think stricter consequences make people less likely to fight?
